story: In July 1969, President John F. Kennedy's goal was realized when Apollo 11 launched atop a Saturn V rocket from Florida. Astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin descended to the lunar surface in the Lunar Module Eagle while Michael Collins orbited aboard Columbia. Upon touchdown on July 20, Armstrong became the first human to step onto the Moon, famously declaring the moment a giant leap for mankind. Immediately after stepping onto the lunar dust, Armstrong gathered a contingency soil sample to ensure scientists back home received lunar material even if an emergency aborted the mission early. Together, Armstrong and Aldrin spent about two and a half hours on the surface, planting an American flag and receiving a historic telephone call from President Richard Nixon in the White House. Watched live by hundreds of millions of Earth viewers, the crew safely completed their moonwalk and splashed down in the Pacific Ocean.
angle: Neil Armstrong's very first action upon stepping onto the Moon was gathering a quick contingency soil sample so humanity would not return empty-handed if an emergency forced an immediate abort.

claims.claim: President John F. Kennedy set a national goal in May 1961 to land a human on the Moon before the end of the 1960s.
Apollo 11 launched from Florida atop a Saturn V rocket.
Neil Armstrong served as the Commander of the Apollo 11 mission.
Buzz Aldrin served as the Lunar Module Pilot for Apollo 11.
Michael Collins was the Command Module Pilot who remained in lunar orbit aboard Columbia.
Armstrong and Aldrin landed the Lunar Module Eagle on the Moon on July 20, 1969.
Neil Armstrong became the first human to step onto the lunar surface.
Armstrong stated 'That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind' upon stepping onto the lunar surface.
Neil Armstrong collected a contingency soil sample shortly after stepping onto the lunar surface.
The contingency sample was collected to ensure lunar material was secured in case an emergency forced an early departure.
Hundreds of millions of television viewers on Earth watched the lunar landing broadcast live.
Armstrong and Aldrin spent about two and a half hours conducting activities on the lunar surface.
The astronauts planted an American flag on the lunar surface.
President Richard Nixon spoke with the astronauts on the Moon via a telephone transmission from the White House.
The Apollo 11 crew returned safely to Earth by splashing down in the Pacific Ocean.

disputed: Whether Neil Armstrong spoke the word 'a' in 'one small step for [a] man'; script should present the quote standardly or note the audio ambiguity.
The exact number of global television viewers (600 million per S1 vs 500 million per S3); script should state 'an estimated 500 to 600 million viewers'.
The exact surface EVA duration (2.5 hours in S1/S5, 2.25 hours in S7, 2.75 hours limit in S4); script should describe it as 'around two and a half hours'.
